image.description: [Home Assistant Core](https://www.home-assistant.io/) - Open source home automation that puts local control and privacy first. Powered by a worldwide community of tinkerers and DIY enthusiasts. Perfect to run on a Raspberry Pi or a local server

changelog.desc: Rebase to alpine 3.24.
Remove pycups as there are no python 3.14 wheels for it.
Rebase to alpine 3.22, rely on baseimage service for usb device permission fixing.
Add the necessary capabilities in the container to allow the unprivileged user access to bluetooth stack.
Rebase to alpine 3.21.
Make setcap target dynamic.
Add go2rtc binary.
Allow uv to modify system python packages.
Switch to `uv` instead of `pip`.
Rebase to alpine 3.20.
Add mime.types to help with detection of certain media files.

Rebase to alpine 3.19, upgrade to python 3.12. Restructure python packages so all packages are internal (no more venv in /config). Use upstream project's wheels. Due to an upstream issue, on first start of the newly updated container, some custom integrations may be disabled in HA due to missing dependencies. A subsequent container restart should fix that and the integrations should be re-enabled.
Add Bluetooth instructions to readme.
Deprecate armhf. As announced [here](https://www.linuxserver.io/blog/a-farewell-to-arm-hf)
Pin pycups version.
Create secondary venv in `/config` for pip installs.
Rebase to alpine 3.18, switch to cp311 wheels.
Deprecate arm32v7. Latest HA version with an arm32v7 build is `2023.4.6`.
Fix the dep conflict for google calendar.
Migrate to s6v3.
Improve usb device permission fix.
Rebase to alpine 3.16, switch to cp310 wheels.
Build matplotlib with the same Numpy version as HA req.
Install pycups.
Install PySwitchbot.
Update pip and use legacy resolver, clean up temp python files, reduce image size.
Always compile grpcio on arm32v7 due to pypi pushing a glibc only wheel.
Use the new `build.yaml` to determine HA base version.
Use the new lsio homeassistant wheel repo, instead of the HA wheels.
Build psycopg locally as the HA provided wheel does not seem to work properly.
Fix setcap in service. Build CISO8601 locally as the HA provided wheel does not seem to work properly.
Rebase to alpine 3.14. Build on native armhf.
Fixed broken build caused by missing dependency.
Remove HACS dependencies as it caused a crash in Home-assistant.
Add python dependencies from homeassistant base image.
Fix building from the wrong requirement file. Add ssh client & external DB libs.
Add iputils so ping works as non root user.
Initial Release.

image.title: Homeassistant
image.setup_instructions:
This image is based on Home Assistant Core.

The Webui can be found at `http://your-ip:8123`. Follow the wizard to set up Home Assistant.

### Host vs. Bridge

Home Assistant can [discover][hb0] and automatically configure
[zeroconf][hb1]/[mDNS][hb2] and [UPnP][hb3] devices on your network. In
order for this to work you must create the container with `--net=host`.

[hb0]: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/discovery/#mdns-and-upnp
[hb1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-configuration_networking
[hb2]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicast_DNS
[hb3]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Plug_and_Play

### Accessing Bluetooth Device

In order to provide HA with access to the host's Bluetooth device, one needs to install BlueZ on the host, add the capabilities `NET_ADMIN` and `NET_RAW` to the container, and map dbus as a volume as shown in the below examples.

#### Docker Cli:
```bash
--cap-add=NET_ADMIN --cap-add=NET_RAW -v /run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro
```

#### Docker Compose:
```yaml
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
      - NET_RAW
    volumes:
      - /run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro
```

If the dbus path on host differs, such as `/var/run/dbus`, then you can map it as `/var/run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro`.

### Using the Ping integration

For the [Ping][ping0] integration to work, the capability `NET_RAW` must be added to the container. See above for instructions.

[ping0]: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ping

snippets.docker_compose:
---
services:
  homeassistant:
    image: ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/homeassistant:latest
    container_name: homeassistant
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=Etc/UTC
    volumes:
      - /path/to/homeassistant/data:/config
    ports:
      - 8123:8123 #optional
    devices:
      - /dev/ttyUSB0:/dev/ttyUSB0 #optional
    restart: unless-stopped
snippets.docker_run:
docker run -d \
  --name=homeassistant \
  --net=host \
  -e PUID=1000 \
  -e PGID=1000 \
  -e TZ=Etc/UTC \
  -p 8123:8123 `#optional` \
  -v /path/to/homeassistant/data:/config \
  --device /dev/ttyUSB0:/dev/ttyUSB0 `#optional` \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  ghcr.io/linuxserver-playground/homeassistant:latest
